scene.description: Outdoor residential exterior in warm Californian late-morning light. Subject occupies the left ~50% of the frame, walking across a residential driveway carrying a window frame, partial three-quarter view, real-world install-in-progress feel — not a posed studio portrait. Right ~50% of frame is occupied by a clean white rendered Google review card overlaying the same exterior background. A circular 35 YEARS anniversary ribbon-seal sits in the bottom-left corner. A row of 5 yellow stars sits across the bottom-right above clean negative space where the CDW wordmark lockup will be composited in Canva post-generation — render that area as natural continuation of the surrounding exterior background, no placeholder box, no dashed outline, no white wordmark zone marker. Mood: warm craftsman, lived-in, real installer at work — never showroom polish, never sterile.
scene.subject: Mike Marohnic (founder, identity supplied by attached mike_founder.png reference photo). Scene/composition: installer in warm casual workwear (long-sleeve shirt, work pants, tool belt visible) carrying or working on a window frame in a residential exterior context. Three-quarters angle, partial view, hands visible, body language reads as a real person mid-task. NO facial features described in this JSON — facial identity is inherited from the attached reference photo per Path D.
scene.setting: Southern California residential exterior — driveway or front-of-house, beige/stucco siding visible in soft focus, warm late-morning light. No recognizable house number, no readable street sign, no specific neighborhood signage.
scene.action: Walking across driveway carrying a window frame, OR adjusting/holding a window frame at eye level in residential exterior context. Static or near-static — installer-mid-task feel, not action sports.

style.primary: editorial trade-credibility portrait + product-still composite — clones REF-001's installer-walking-with-window-frame pose at left + review-card-overlay at right
style.rendering_quality: hyperrealistic photographic, slight phone-photo realism, no Instagram filter, no luxury-mansion gloss
style.surface_textures: natural skin texture (pores, hair, slight late-morning sheen — supplied by attached reference photo), workwear fabric weave, metal/aluminum window-frame edge, beige stucco siding, asphalt driveway micro-texture
style.lighting: natural late-morning Californian daylight ~5200K, warm cast, golden-hour edge bias on subject's left side, soft diffuse fill on the right (review-card side) to keep card readability high

camera.focal_length: 50mm equivalent — avoid wide-angle distortion that signals stock photography
camera.aperture: f/4 — subject sharp; background gently softened; review card on right remains crisp and readable
camera.depth_of_field: moderate — subject and review card both in acceptable focus; deep background softened
camera.angle: eye level, slightly off-axis to match REF-001's installer-walking framing

technical.resolution: 1440x1800 mobile-first 4:5 vertical (Meta Feed / Reels / IG Feed)
technical.rendering: Editorial finish, real-photo authenticity, no heavy color grade. Warm Californian craft palette per CDW design system (sun-yellow + warm red accents, off-white, soft black).

materials.surfaces: Aluminum or vinyl window-frame in subject's hands — clean fresh-fabricated, not weathered. Driveway asphalt + beige stucco siding in background. Reflective platform NONE.
materials.transparency: Window-frame glass shows light reflection consistent with daylight scene; no jarring artificial highlights.

environment.particles: Faint sun-warmed atmospheric haze acceptable; no dust storms, no smoke, no bokeh-balls.

spec.verbatim_review_body_preferred_full_text: We had doors replaced about 6 years ago by a 'virtual' outfit and it turned into constant repairs, service calls, and headaches once the warranty ended. This time we wanted a real local company... when you call, a real person picks up and gets things handled. No 'press 1, press 4, press 8' maze.
spec.truncation_fallback_if_needed: We had doors replaced about 6 years ago by a 'virtual' outfit and it turned into constant repairs... This time we wanted a real local company... when you call, a real person picks up and gets things handled. No 'press 1, press 4, press 8' maze.
spec.visual_focal_point_sentence: When you call, a real person picks up and gets things handled. No 'press 1, press 4, press 8' maze.
spec.focal_point_treatment: The rendered card must keep the full body legible, but the visual hierarchy of the card should make the focal-point sentence the most readable focal point — through scale, weight, position within the card, or natural truncation that lands this sentence at the readable midpoint.
spec.verbatim_accuracy_lock: Per Agent 9 CLONE MODE Path 2 guardrail: review text and reviewer details are EXACT, not paraphrased. If at generation time any rendered detail differs from this spec (a word changes, 'virtual' becomes 'online', 'press 1, press 4, press 8' is altered, the date drifts, the avatar renders an initial letter, the platform mark is wrong), the variation FAILS Agent 9 review and must be regenerated. Path 2 is for visual rendering of REAL content — never for fabricating reviews.
